system_description.narrative_title: France's unrest and sovereign stress destabilize global bond markets
system_description.narrative_summary: Widespread protests and political turmoil in France are raising sovereign-risk premia, driving French yields sharply higher and prompting ratings scrutiny. That domestic shock is transmitting through open financial channels to FX and global bond markets — investors pivot to perceived safe havens (US Treasuries, yen), creating volatility and forcing reassessments by central banks and market participants. The system is open: domestic political events alter investor expectations and cross-border capital flows, which in turn feed back into funding costs, currency moves, and policy signaling across jurisdictions.
system_description.scope: Within the boundary: French political stability and protest dynamics; France sovereign and corporate debt markets (yields, spreads, ratings reviews); investor flows into/out of French and eurozone debt; contagion effects on eurozone sovereigns; FX moves involving euro, yen, dollar; reactions in global bond markets and short-term central bank policy signaling.
system_description.super_system: Global financial system and macroeconomic environment (cross-border capital markets, international monetary policy, global risk sentiment)
adjacent_subsystems: Eurozone sovereign debt dynamics (Italy, Spain, peripheral spreads)
US Treasury market and dollar safe-haven flows
Central bank policy decisions and global interest-rate expectations

variables.name: Political unrest intensity
variables.description: Measures the scale, frequency, and severity of domestic protests and civil disturbances affecting public order.

variables.name: Sovereign risk premium
variables.description: Measures the additional yield investors demand over a benchmark for holding a sovereign's debt, reflecting perceived default and political risk.

variables.name: Sovereign bond yield level
variables.description: Level of long-term sovereign government bond yields as priced by markets.

variables.name: Corporate credit spreads
variables.description: Average spread between corporate bond yields and comparable sovereign yields, capturing corporate credit risk and liquidity premia.

variables.name: Cross-border capital flows
variables.description: Net flow of capital moving across borders into or out of sovereign and corporate debt markets.

variables.name: Safe-haven asset demand
variables.description: Investor demand for assets perceived as safe that drives reallocations away from riskier holdings.

variables.name: Major currency exchange rates
variables.description: Relative values and movements of major currencies against one another, reflecting capital flows and risk sentiment.

variables.name: Global bond market volatility
variables.description: Realized and implied volatility in global sovereign and corporate bond markets indicating uncertainty and price swings.

variables.name: Policy rate expectations
variables.description: Market-implied expectations of future central bank policy rates across major jurisdictions.

variables.name: Credit rating pressure
variables.description: Market-implied likelihood and upward/downward pressure on sovereign credit ratings and associated perceptions of creditworthiness.

variables.name: Market liquidity
variables.description: Depth and ease of executing trades in bond markets, reflected in bid-ask spreads, market depth, and trade impact.

variables.name: Short-term funding spreads
variables.description: Spreads and costs in short-term wholesale funding markets that determine banks' and intermediaries' borrowing costs.

variables.name: Investor risk aversion
variables.description: Degree to which investors prefer lower-risk assets, influencing demand across asset classes and premium levels.

variables.name: Contagion transmission intensity
variables.description: Speed and intensity with which financial stress or risk perception spreads between sovereign debt markets and across borders.

variables.name: Yield curve slope
variables.description: Difference between long-term and short-term sovereign yields, capturing term-premia and expectations about future rates and growth.

variables.name: Portfolio rebalancing rate
variables.description: Rate at which investors adjust allocations between domestic and foreign bonds and between risk tiers in response to shocks.
